title: SMC POI Zones — FVG, Order Block & QML Level

poi_zones_overview.llm_summary: Point of Interest (POI) zones are the specific price levels where smart money traders look for trade entries. There are exactly 3 types of POI zones: (1) Fair Value Gap (FVG), (2) Order Block (OB), and (3) QML Level (Quasimodo Level). These three zones serve as the entry mechanisms after identifying market structure, liquidity, and inducement. FVG is the highest priority, Order Block is second priority, and QML Level is third priority (used as confluence when FVG and OB are not available). The presenter reviews FVG and OB concepts from previous videos and introduces QML Level as a new concept in this video.
key_rules: POI (Point of Interest) = specific price zones where smart money enters trades
3 types of POI zones: FVG, Order Block, QML Level
Priority ranking: FVG (1st) → Order Block (2nd) → QML Level (3rd)
QML Level is used as confluence entry when no FVG or OB is available
POI zones are the ENTRY mechanism — used after identifying structure, liquidity, inducement

fvg_review.llm_summary: Fair Value Gap (FVG) is the refined form of Liquidity Void or Price Imbalance — the area where price moves sharply in one direction, leaving pending orders behind as liquidity. FVG is specifically measured as the wick-to-wick gap between the 1st and 3rd candle (not the bodies). A valid FVG occurs when there is a clear gap between the wick of candle 1 and the wick of candle 3, with the middle candle (candle 2) being the expansion candle. Inside candles do NOT create valid FVGs because there is no genuine imbalance. FVG is the HIGHEST priority POI zone because it represents the purest form of price imbalance where smart money has unmitigated orders.
key_rules: FVG = Refined Form of Liquidity Void or Price Imbalance
FVG = Wick-to-Wick Gap between 1st and 3rd candle
Area where price moves sharply in one direction, leaving pending orders behind
Inside candle FVG = NOT important (no genuine imbalance)
FVG is HIGHEST priority POI zone (1st priority)
FVG represents the purest form of price imbalance with unmitigated SM orders

order_block_review.llm_summary: Order Block is a refined form of Institutional Order Flow (IOF) — the collection of pending orders of big banks and institutions distributed in block form. Every buy candle before a sell move is a Bearish Order Block; every sell candle before a buy move is a Bullish Order Block. For an OB to be valid, two rules must be satisfied: (1) the candle must sweep liquidity of the previous candle or previous high/low, and (2) a price imbalance (FVG) must exist below/above the candle's wick. Inside candles are NOT valid pullbacks and therefore cannot form valid OBs. OBs that are part of inducement or engineered liquidity become Smart Money Traps — market will break through them. Order Block is the 2nd priority POI zone after FVG.
key_rules: Order Block = refined form of IOF = collection of pending orders of big banks
Bearish OB = buy candle before sell move; Bullish OB = sell candle before buy move
Valid OB Rule 1: candle MUST sweep liquidity of previous candle or previous high/low
Valid OB Rule 2: price imbalance (FVG) MUST exist below/above the candle's wick
Inside candle = NOT valid pullback → cannot form valid OB
OB in inducement/engineered liquidity zone = Smart Money Trap (market breaks through)

qml_level_definition.llm_summary: QML Level (Quasimodo Level, also called QM-Level) is a price level where market sweeps liquidity above/below a high/low and then moves sharply in the opposite direction. The name comes from Disney's Quasimodo character — the pattern resembles uneven shoulders (one shoulder higher than the other), similar to Quasimodo's hunchback. Bearish QML: In a bullish move, price makes a higher high (sweeping liquidity above the previous high with a liquidity grab), then reverses with a Market Structure Shift (MSS — candle body closes below the corresponding low). The horizontal line drawn at the swept high becomes the QML Level. When price returns to this level, it provides a sell entry. Bullish QML: In a bearish move, price makes a lower low (sweeping liquidity below the previous low), then reverses with MSS upward. The horizontal line at the swept low becomes the QML Level for buy entry. QML is the 3rd priority POI zone — used when no valid FVG or OB is available. QML provides excellent risk/reward ratio and becomes high probability when inducement is also available at the level. QML can align with IOF (Institutional Order Flow) baseline for even stronger confluence.
key_rules: QML Level (Quasimodo Level) = level where market sweeps liquidity and moves sharply opposite
Named after Disney's Quasimodo — pattern resembles uneven shoulders (one higher than other)
Bearish QML: price sweeps high's liquidity (liquidity grab) → MSS below corresponding low → horizontal line at swept high = QML
Bullish QML: price sweeps low's liquidity → MSS above corresponding high → horizontal line at swept low = QML
MSS (Market Structure Shift) = candle body must CLOSE beyond the key level (not just wick)
QML is 3rd priority POI zone — used when no valid FVG or OB available
QML provides excellent risk/reward ratio
High probability when inducement is also available at QML level
QML can align with IOF baseline for stronger confluence
Draw horizontal line at the exact price where liquidity was swept = QML entry level

entry_workflow_with_poi.llm_summary: The complete entry workflow using POI zones follows a strict sequence: (1) NEVER trade the first POI zone directly — it will likely be used as inducement/liquidity. (2) Wait for price to reach a POI zone and create inducement. (3) Wait for a Market Structure Shift (MSS) — candle body must close beyond the key structural level. (4) After the shift, identify the NEW POI zone that forms (FVG, OB, or QML). (5) Trade the new zone, not the original one. The presenter demonstrates two complete real-chart examples: (A) USD/CAD M30 bullish trade — identifies QML level that aligns with IOF baseline, waits for inducement + shift, enters at the new zone with approximately 1:5 risk-reward. (B) AUD/USD M15 bearish trade — identifies BOS (Break of Structure) at top, recognizes IDM/SMT zone (inducement/smart money trap where retail OBs get broken), waits for internal liquidity sweep + shift, identifies QML Level as the POI entry, market respects QML and drops significantly. Key insight: OBs below inducement in a sell trend are Smart Money Traps — retail gets stopped out. Use QML as the POI when OBs are trapped.

Wait for inducement to form at the POI zone before considering entry

Trade the new zone formed AFTER the shift, not the original zone
OBs below inducement in sell trend = Smart Money Traps — retail gets stopped out
When OBs are trapped, use QML Level as the POI entry
QML aligned with IOF baseline = very high probability confluence
Internal liquidity sweeps within the structure provide additional confirmation
Complete workflow: Structure → Liquidity → Inducement → Shift → New POI → Entry
